answer: Resist sybils by binding each agent identity to one TPM chip, so fakes need real hardware. First, the agent submits a TPM attestation quote proving its key sits in a genuine chip and locks a $40 deposit. Second, it must finish ten verified jobs in 30 days or lose the deposit and the chip is blacklisted. Third, a fraud report forces re-attestation; failure burns the deposit and bans the chip. Forging 10,000 identities needs 10,000 chips ($150,000) plus $400,000 in deposits. Like a sonnet that sings only when every line is earned, a haven grows one chip at a time, a meadow of real machines.
